details.description: Amazon Nova Lite is Amazon's low-cost multimodal foundation model, launched December 5, 2024 and accessed through Amazon Bedrock. It processes text and image inputs and generates text output, with a 300K-token context window, and also accepts document inputs such as PDF, DOCX and XLS. It supports the Converse API, client-side tool calling and fine-tuning, and Amazon positions it for interactive chat, retrieval-augmented generation, agentic applications and UI workflow automation. AWS's Bedrock model card lists this v1 snapshot as Active, with no end-of-life date announced as of this research.
advantages: Accepts document inputs including PDF, CSV, DOC, DOCX, XLS, XLSX, HTML, TXT and MD files (Amazon Nova user guide).
Supports explicit prompt caching, with a minimum of 1K tokens per cache checkpoint and up to 4 checkpoints per request, to reduce latency and cost on repeated context (AWS Bedrock model card).
Supports client-side tool calling and Amazon Bedrock Agents for building agentic workflows (AWS Bedrock model card).
Optimized for 15 named languages within a training set Amazon says spans up to 200 languages (Amazon Nova user guide).
disadvantages: Does not support structured outputs via the bedrock-runtime API (AWS Bedrock model card).
Knowledge cutoff of October 2024 (AWS Bedrock model card).
Amazon's Nova documentation site now covers this as 'Amazon Nova Version 1' and points to a separate Nova 2 user guide, and AWS's Bedrock model catalog separately lists a newer 'Nova 2 Lite' model.
use_cases: Agentic applications and UI workflow automation
Document analysis and visual question answering

notes: Catalog's max_output_tokens (10000) matches the Nova user guide's model-specifications table (10K), but AWS's Bedrock model card for amazon.nova-lite-v1:0 separately states 'Max output tokens: 5K' -- kept the catalog's value and flagged this source disagreement. AWS's own documentation also lists video as a supported input modality for Nova Lite alongside text and image, but the catalog's modality facts list only text_input, image_input and text_output, so video input was left out of the write-up per the catalog's authoritative facts. Found no accuracy-style benchmark scores from Amazon or a named leaderboard for this exact model.
